text: Let p and q be two propositions. Consider the following two formulae in propositional logic. S1: (¬p∧(p∨q))→q and S2: q→(¬p∧(p∨q)). Which one of the following choices is correct?
options: Both S1 and S2 are tautologies.
S1 is a tautology but S2 is not a tautology
S1 is not a tautology but S2 is a tautology
Neither S1 nor S2 is a tautology
solution: S1: ¬p∧(p∨q) ≡ ¬p∧q, so S1 ≡ (¬p∧q)→q ≡ p∨¬q∨q ≡ T. S2: q→(¬p∧q) ≡ ¬q∨(¬p∧q) ≡ ¬q∨¬p, which is false when p=q=T. So S1 is a tautology and S2 is not.
